posts.hook: When two crews work together, I blend their stations. You can hear the alliance.
posts.script:
Here's something I'm properly excited about for the night.
When two crews work together on screen, I blend their two stations. A swing vocal over a Miami synth. A G-funk beat under an old crooner.
So you don't just watch an alliance happen — you hear the turf mixing, in real time, in the room.
And when the alliance breaks, so does the mix.
That's not a gimmick. That's the whole reason to do this live instead of just playing you a film.
The room is an instrument that night.
shots: two records, two colour washes, blending
a crowd under two colliding colours
posts.caption: When they ally, I blend their stations. When it breaks, so does the mix.
posts.shareTrigger: Craft flex — justifies the ticket price without saying so.

posts.title: One Month
posts.hook: One month out. If you've been here since the docks, you know more than most people in that room.
posts.script:
One month.
If you've been with this since the docks and the four signatures, you now know things that most of the people standing in that room won't.
You know why there are four keys. You know the window's four minutes. You know what the flowers mean, or at least you know they mean something.
All of that is going to be useful.
Because on the night, when everybody else is working out what's happening, you'll already be playing.
One month. Pick your colour.
shots: a calendar, one date circled
a lit venue exterior, night, wet street
posts.caption: One month. You already know more than most people who'll be in that room.
posts.shareTrigger: Rewards long-term followers; makes lurkers commit.

posts.title: He's Been Here
posts.hook: McGraw found something in that cemetery. He's stopped going.
posts.script:
McGraw's stopped going to the cemetery.
He went every year on that date for eleven years, sat in the rain, waited for somebody who never came.
He's stopped.
Not because he gave up — I've never seen the man more awake than he's been this month. Because something about that grave stopped being a question.
He's got a name now. Or he's got half of one.
And for the first time in twenty years, Dutch McGraw is not the one being led around this city.
He's ahead.
shots: an empty cemetery, wet flowers, no one
a detective walking away from a grave
posts.caption: Eleven years he sat in that cemetery. This year he didn't go.
posts.cta: He's ahead. For the first time.
posts.shareTrigger: Pays off day 48 — long-arc payoff builds serial loyalty.

posts.title: On The Night
posts.hook: What to actually expect, start to finish, no mystique.
posts.script:
No mystique for one post. Just what happens.
You arrive, you get a colour, you get a link on your phone. There's music. About half an hour in, the story starts on the screens.
From there it's music, story, game, music — twelve games across the night, all played on your phone, all scoring for your crew.
The last one is the vault and it's the loudest thing you'll do all year.
Then we count it, somebody wins, and the music goes back up until they throw us out.
That's it. That's the night.
shots: a full run of the room, wide, colour-lit
a leaderboard, four colours climbing
posts.caption: No mystique. That's the whole night, start to finish.
posts.cta: Any questions, ask below — I answer all of them.
posts.shareTrigger: Clarity converts; the Q&A replies become more content.

posts.title: Fifty Years To The Day
posts.hook: The gala is fifty years to the week from the day four men signed that document.
posts.script:
One last piece of history before we get into the night itself.
That gala, in November, falls fifty years almost to the week from the day those four men sat in a back room and signed a document that made all of this inevitable.
That could be a coincidence.
The President's office says it's a coincidence.
But somebody chose that date, and somebody added a fifth name to the guest list, and somebody has been sending white flowers to an unmarked grave every year for four decades.
I don't think anything about November is a coincidence.
I think somebody's been planning it for fifty years.
shots: an old document beside a new invitation
a calendar, two dates, fifty years apart
posts.caption: Fifty years to the week. His office says coincidence.
posts.shareTrigger: Ties the whole serial together — the pre-countdown peak.

posts.title: Three Weeks
posts.hook: Three weeks. Everybody in this story is now doing something they can't undo.
posts.script:
Three weeks.
Everybody in this story has now done something they can't take back. Keys have moved. RSVPs are in. A detective has a name he won't say out loud.
There's no version of November where these four crews quietly decide not to bother.
And there's no version where they manage it without people on the floor.
So here's where you come in, one more time, plainly.
Pick a colour. Get a ticket. Turn up early.
The rest of it I'll handle on the night.
shots: four cars on four wet streets
a venue exterior, lights coming on
posts.caption: Three weeks. Nobody can call it off now.
posts.cta: Colour + ticket. That's the whole ask.
posts.shareTrigger: Urgency without a fake deadline.

posts.title: The Crews Are Moving
posts.hook: All four crews changed their behaviour this month. Here's how you'd spot it.
posts.script:
All four crews have changed behaviour this month and none of them think it's visible.
The Corvettis stopped taking meetings. The Halcóns started throwing parties, which for them is camouflage.
The Street Kings moved every car off the block.
And The Firm filed three separate insurance policies in one week, which is the single most Firm thing that has ever happened.
Four organisations preparing for the same night in four completely different languages.
All of them convinced they're the only one who's ready.
shots: four districts, four kinds of activity
a chess-like grid of four colours
posts.caption: Four crews prepping in four different languages. All think they're alone.
posts.shareTrigger: Comparison prompt — factions argue their own corner.

posts.title: Last Words
posts.hook: "If it goes wrong in there, get to the water." Somebody's already planning to lose.
posts.script:
Overheard this week, from a senior man to somebody much younger:
If it goes wrong in there, don't go for a door. Get to the water.
Think about what that tells you.
Somebody in one of these four crews has already sat down and planned for the version where they don't get the money and they don't get out the front.
That's not pessimism. That's the most professional thing anybody's said in months.
Everybody else is planning to win.
One of them is planning to survive.
shots: dark water at night, a distant boat
a fire exit, red light, wet floor
posts.caption: "If it goes wrong, get to the water." Somebody's planning to lose.
posts.shareTrigger: Dread + a guessing game — very high comment volume.

posts.title: The Signal
posts.hook: There's one sound in this whole night that doesn't belong to any crew.
posts.script:
There's one sound on that dial that doesn't belong to any crew.
It comes in over the top of whatever's playing — cuts across gold, pink, cyan and violet like none of them are there — and when it does, the room goes quiet without being asked.
I've built it as a loop. Low, slow, a bit seductive, a bit wrong.
You'll hear it in the first ten minutes.
You'll hear it again at the very end.
And what happens in between those two moments is the entire reason to be in that room.
shots: a radio dial warping between stations
a dark room, one low light, quiet crowd
posts.caption: One sound that doesn't belong to any crew. You'll hear it twice.
posts.shareTrigger: Musical mystery — a payoff people attend to receive.

posts.title: Last Chance
posts.hook: McGraw's been told to drop it. In writing. For the third time.
posts.script:
McGraw's been told to drop it. Formally, in writing, third time in twenty years.
He's two years off a pension he's already been told won't be full.
And he's going to be at that gala. Not officially — he's not on the list, he wasn't invited, and if he's recognised he'll be walked out and probably finished.
He's going anyway.
Everybody else in that room is going for eight figures.
He's going for a name.
Of every person walking into that building in November, he's the only one risking something he can't get back.
shots: a memo, stamped, on a cluttered desk
a lone figure outside a lit venue, rain
posts.caption: Told to drop it. Third time. He's going anyway.
posts.shareTrigger: Rooting interest at peak — sets up the post-credit payoff.

posts.title: Final Logistics
posts.hook: Doors, ID, phone charged, colour chosen. That's the whole checklist.
posts.script:
Final checklist, then I'll stop being practical at you.
Bring ID. Charge your phone — properly, not to forty percent.
Get there for doors, because the open sets up everything and the first game scores.
And know your colour before you're standing at that desk with people behind you.
That's it. Four things.
Everything else that night is handled — by me, from the booth, all night.
You just have to turn up ready to be somebody's soldier.
shots: a phone at 100%, neon reflection
a door, four coloured lights, queue
posts.caption: ID. Charged phone. Doors. Colour. That's the list.
posts.shareTrigger: Explicitly saveable — a checklist gets kept and re-shared.

posts.title: From Here
posts.hook: From tomorrow I stop telling you history and start telling you who you're about to meet.
posts.script:
From tomorrow this changes.
I'm done with the history. Fifty years, four families, one document, one grave — you've got all of it, and it's going to matter more than you think.
From here I'm introducing you to the people you're actually going to be in a room with. The four bosses. The ones standing behind them. The detective. The president.
And then the games, one at a time, so you know exactly how to win them.
Three weeks of that, and then doors.
Stay tuned in.
shots: a radio dial settling on one station
TJ to camera, hard key, black three-piece
posts.caption: History's done. From tomorrow: who you're about to meet.
posts.shareTrigger: Momentum handoff into the countdown run.

posts.title: The Corvettis
posts.hook: The oldest crew in this city has never raised its voice. Not once.
posts.script:
The Corvettis got here first. Off the boats, onto the docks, into the restaurants, and eventually into everything — quietly, over three generations, one favour at a time.
Don Salvatore Corvetti runs them the way his father did. Nothing written down. Nothing said twice. A back room behind a restaurant where the light is always warm and the conversation is always short.
Their whole economy is respect. The money is just how they keep score.
They hold the gold key. They've held it for fifty years.
And they have never once had to ask for anything twice.
shots: gold-lit waterfront, wet cobbles, fog
warm gold back room, checkered cloth
a gold pinky ring, macro
posts.caption: Three generations. Nothing written down. GOLD — the Corvettis. #GTAD
posts.shareTrigger: Faction recruitment — the first of four; people start claiming.

posts.title: The Don
posts.hook: He was asked what the drop was. He ate a cannoli and thought about it for a full ten seconds.
posts.script:
Don Salvatore Corvetti. Sally Cufflinks. Past seventy-five, and he has never once raised his voice, because he has never had to.
His son Vinnie sweats through every shirt he owns and asks questions the Don finds exhausting.
So the Don tells him: take the product. Don't look at the product. Don't talk about the product. Move it, and make the drop.
And Vinnie — God help him — asks what the drop is.
The old man eats a cannoli. Thinks about it. Long enough that it gets uncomfortable.
And he says: respect. And also the drop.
shots: elderly don at a table, gold light, quiet menace
a cannoli, macro, warm
a sweating man in an open collar
posts.caption: "Pop… what's the drop?" — a question you only ask once.
posts.cta: Tag the Vinnie in your crew.
posts.shareTrigger: Tag-a-friend: the character is a person everyone knows.

posts.title: Los Halcóns
posts.hook: This crew has never hidden anything in their lives and they're not going to start now.
posts.script:
Los Halcóns came up through the marina in the eighties, and they did not come up quietly.
Where the Corvettis hide, the Halcóns announce. White suits. Neon on the water. A mansion you can see from the bridge and a tiger in the front room.
Rico Delgado believes the loudest crew wins, and for twenty years he's been proven right often enough to never seriously consider the alternative.
If you have to ask whether something in this city is theirs — it isn't.
They hold the pink key.
They'd like everyone to know that.
shots: hot-pink neon marina, black yachts, palms
mirrored mansion glowing through rain
a gold falcon medallion, macro
posts.caption: If you have to ask whether it's theirs, it isn't. PINK — Los Halcóns.
posts.shareTrigger: Faction rivalry: directly baits the gold crew.

posts.title: Rico
posts.hook: Somebody shot at Rico Delgado in his own house and he did not blink. He was insulted.
posts.script:
Rico Delgado. El Halcón. What happens when confidence stops asking permission.
White linen suit open to the middle of his chest. A gold falcon on a chain. A scar over one eyebrow. And a full-grown Bengal tiger named Sugar who lies on the white couch and does not care about any of this.
Somebody sent targets to his house. A round went past his cheek — close enough to feel it — and he did not blink.
He wasn't frightened. He was insulted.
He turned to the tiger and said: you believe this? After everything I do for this city?
shots: white suit inside a storm of neon tracer fire
tiger on a white couch, unbothered
mirrors and muzzle-flash, no faces
posts.caption: "You believe this, Sugar? After everything I do for this city?"
posts.cta: Which crew would you actually survive in?
posts.shareTrigger: Disbelief + humour — the tiger does the sharing.

posts.title: The Street Kings
posts.hook: Everyone gets this crew wrong. They never wanted the city.
posts.script:
Everybody gets the Street Kings wrong.
They never wanted the city. That's the part the other three can't process.
Marcus Wells wanted the block — and the block is what he has. Every corner of it. Loyal. And nobody had to be frightened into it.
They're the only crew in this whole story that people join because they actually want to.
Cars, corners, hydraulics and the coolest three minutes of music in any room they walk into.
They hold the cyan key.
And if this whole thing goes wrong, they're the crew you want standing next to you.
shots: cyan-lit block, chrome lowrider on hydraulics
murals, corner-store glow, wet asphalt
a convoy pulling into neon night
posts.caption: The only crew people join because they want to. CYAN.
posts.shareTrigger: Underdog identity: the sympathetic pick, easy to champion.

posts.title: Marcus
posts.hook: Four cop cars in the mirror and this man's only problem is his passenger.
posts.script:
Marcus Wells. Big Deal. The calmest man in this entire story.
Fresh fade. One gold chain. A chrome-and-cyan lowrider sitting on hydraulics. Marcus has never needed to prove anything to anybody, which is exactly why nobody tries him.
One cop in the mirror. Then four. Then a helicopter.
And riding shotgun is Lil' Problem, who has not noticed any of this, because he is deep into a plan for a taco empire funded entirely by money nobody has stolen yet.
Marcus doesn't raise his voice either. He just says: Problem. Put the taco down and drive.
shots: POV windshield, neon rushing, police lights behind
lowrider peeling out, low tracking
rear-view mirror full of red-blue
posts.caption: One cop. Then four. Then a helicopter. And Problem's still talking about tacos.
posts.shareTrigger: Relatable duo — the comedy travels further than the lore.

posts.title: The Firm
posts.hook: The newest crew in this city bought their way in, and nobody has forgiven them for it.
posts.script:
The Firm bought their way in.
No history. No neighbourhood. No bodies. Just a glass tower, a great deal of other people's money, and a founder who will tell you at length that he has reinvented theft.
They're the newest crew, the richest crew, and by a considerable margin the least liked.
The other three call them tourists. The Firm calls the other three legacy infrastructure.
They hold the violet key. They also have a slide deck about the violet key.
And here's the uncomfortable part: they're not wrong about very much.
shots: cold violet glass towers, one lit floor high up
a wall of surveillance monitors, screen glow
a business card straightened, macro
posts.caption: The other three call them tourists. They call the other three legacy infrastructure.
posts.shareTrigger: Villain faction: people love picking the hated one.

posts.title: Preston
posts.hook: He's reinvented theft. No masks, no guns. He calls it a proprietary infiltration solution.
posts.script:
Preston Ashford Sterling the Third has reinvented theft.
No masks. No guns. Just — his words — a proprietary infiltration solution. He calls it Breach. It is currently in private beta.
He demoed it once. It shrieked in his hands, the room went emergency red, and his analyst Kayleigh — standing on the other side of the bench already holding a defused one — did not look up.
He called it a soft launch.
And when he asked her who in this city was leaking, she said: it's you, Preston. You post everything.
He took that as engagement.
shots: black turtleneck fumbling a wired device
violet room flipping emergency red
an analyst with a tablet, bored, unbothered
posts.caption: "That was a soft launch." #GTAD
posts.cta: Every office has one. Name them.
posts.shareTrigger: Recognition humour — everyone has worked for this man.

posts.title: Vinnie the Veal
posts.hook: This man has one job and he has already asked three questions about it.
posts.script:
Vinnie the Veal. The Don's son. Slicked hair, open collar, gold chain, and a shirt he is sweating through in real time.
Vinnie has one job on the night: move the product, make the drop, don't ask what it is.
So far Vinnie has asked what it is three times.
His father has explained it to him twice, and the second explanation was worse than the first.
I want to be clear that the Corvettis are the most feared crew in this city, and their succession plan is this guy.
shots: a sweating man in an open collar, gold light
a briefcase on a checkered tablecloth
the don's hand, dismissive, macro
posts.caption: The most feared crew in the city. This is the succession plan.
posts.shareTrigger: Family-tag humour — the most re-shareable format there is.

posts.title: Lil' Problem
posts.hook: He's already spent the vault money. In his head. On tacos.
posts.script:
Lil' Problem. Cyan tracksuit, gold rope, permanently mid-sentence, permanently eating.
Problem has already spent the vault money. In his head. On tacos.
Not a taco truck — he wants that on record. A fleet. A taco empire.
He has done no maths on this. He has, however, already picked the name and thought about the logo.
And when someone suggested he might boost the getaway car himself — that it might be his origin story — Marcus had to explain to him, gently, that it's a Honda.
Problem's response: a legendary Honda.
shots: cyan corner, a man mid-laugh holding food
a beat-up Honda under neon, hero angle
hands gesturing a plan, no face
posts.caption: "…A *legendary* Honda."
posts.shareTrigger: Pure comedy clip — the one that escapes the fanbase.

posts.title: Sugar
posts.hook: During a fifty-fifty handshake between two crime families, the tiger robbed both of them.
posts.script:
Two crews. One table. A fifty-fifty split, agreed like brothers, with a handshake neither man was willing to let go of first.
The Don is watching Rico. Rico is watching the Don. Both of them are absolutely certain they're the one doing the outsmarting.
And behind them — completely unnoticed, in no hurry whatsoever — Sugar picks up a bag of money off the table and walks out of the building with it.
A tiger.
Robbed a summit of the two most dangerous men in this city.
Neither of them has noticed yet. I'm not going to be the one to tell them.
shots: two bosses shaking hands, gold vs pink light
a tiger padding out of frame with a gold bag
an empty spot on a table where a bag was
posts.caption: The tiger robbed both crime families and nobody has noticed yet.
posts.cta: Send this to someone who'd get away with it.
posts.shareTrigger: The single most shareable image in the world — an animal outsmarting everyone.

posts.title: Kayleigh
posts.hook: She ended her boss's entire investigation in one sentence and went back to her tablet.
posts.script:
Kayleigh works for The Firm. Sleek low bun, wireless headset, tablet, entirely unbothered.
Preston decided somebody in this city was leaking, and ordered a full loyalty audit. Every crew. Cross-referenced. He wanted to know — and I want to be accurate here — whether they could gamify it. Whether the rat could be a subscription.
Kayleigh looked up exactly once and said: the rat is you, Preston. You post everything.
Then went back to her tablet.
She is paid a fraction of what he is.
She is the only reason that tower is still standing.
shots: analyst at a monitor wall, violet glow
a red target box snapping onto a blurred face
a tablet, one raised eyebrow, no full face
posts.caption: Ended the whole investigation in one sentence. Went back to work.
posts.cta: Tag the Kayleigh holding your workplace together.
posts.shareTrigger: Workplace recognition — huge crossover outside the nightlife audience.

posts.title: McGraw
posts.hook: Twenty years chasing one man, and he has been wrong every single time.
posts.script:
Detective Dutch McGraw. Twenty years, one trench coat, a toothpick, and a wall of faces.
He's hunting a man with no face and a vault with no bottom, and every single year he almost has him.
He'll put five people in a lineup — one from each crew, and one civilian who wandered in off the dance floor holding his booking number upside down — and he will point, with total confidence, at the wrong one.
He always points at the wrong one.
Here's the thing about McGraw, though.
He's the only honest man in this entire story. And it's cost him everything.
shots: venetian blinds, red-blue siren light
a lineup wall in silhouette
a toothpick, a tired face, hard key
posts.caption: Twenty years. Every year he almost has him. #GTAD
posts.cta: Is he ever going to get it right?
posts.shareTrigger: Sympathy + prediction — people theorise in the comments.

posts.title: President Diamante
posts.hook: He says he knows all the criminals personally. That's not a slip. He means it as a boast.
posts.script:
President Maximillian Diamante will tell you this city is safer than it has ever been.
Believe him. He'll say it under a banner that reads WAR ON CRIME, in a room where every single crew in this story is holding a drink.
He says nobody's tougher on crime than him, because he knows all the criminals personally. Great people. Total winners.
That's not a slip of the tongue. He means it as a boast.
And while he's saying it, four envelopes — one gold, one pink, one cyan, one violet — go into his jacket at the same time.
He has never, ever taken a dollar from any of these fine… patrons.
shots: podium under a WAR ON CRIME banner
four coloured envelopes into a jacket, neck-down
a grid of storefront TVs on a wet street
posts.caption: "I know all the criminals personally. Great people."
posts.shareTrigger: Satire — political comedy travels beyond the event audience.

posts.title: The Myth, Again
posts.hook: The Firm has a file on him. I've seen it. There's nothing in it.
posts.script:
I told you about the man with no face. Here's what I've learned since.
The Corvettis are certain he takes a cut of everything — they've been paying something to somebody for three generations and the Don won't say to who.
Rico swears he's been inside the house. Rico has changed the locks four times.
And The Firm has a file on him. I've seen the file.
There is nothing in it.
No photograph. No name. No record of a man who four crews will not make a move without thinking about.
Four keys. Four crews. And all of them frightened of the same empty folder.
shots: a manila file opening on nothing
a black-gloved hand tipping a glass off a podium
a single lit window, rain, very high up
posts.caption: An empty file. Four terrified crime families. Explain that one.
posts.shareTrigger: Mystery participation — comments become the content.

posts.title: How It Actually Works
posts.hook: You don't watch this. Your phone is the controller and you're playing for a gang.
posts.script:
Let me tell you how the night actually runs, because people keep asking.
You get in. You pick a colour at the door — gold, pink, cyan or violet. That's your crew now.
Through the night, the story plays on the screens. It stops. Somebody looks straight down the lens and hands you a job.
And then everybody's phone lights up at once and you play it. Right there. On the floor. Against every other crew in the building.
There's nothing to download at the door and nothing to carry. No props, no lines, no getting picked on stage.
Twelve games. One night. Your colour's on the board the whole time.
shots: a floor of raised phones glowing four colours
a game card hitting the screens
a leaderboard flipping over
posts.caption: Phone up. Pick a colour. Twelve games. #GTAD
posts.shareTrigger: Removes the #1 objection: 'do I have to get on stage?'

posts.title: The Interrogation
posts.hook: The first game of the night is eight questions and a detective who can tell when you're lying.
posts.script:
First game of the night. McGraw's got five of you in a lineup and the whole room watching.
Eight questions. Fast. On your phone.
Answer straight, answer quick, and do not crack — because he's been doing this twenty years and the whole city sees your answer.
It's the easiest game of the night and it's the one people lose, because they get clever.
Top score talks first.
And whoever talks first sets the tone for their crew for the rest of the night.
shots: five suspects in silhouette at a height marker
phones lighting up in the dark
a toothpick jabbed at the lens
posts.caption: Eight questions. Don't get clever. #GTAD
posts.cta: How fast are you under pressure?
posts.shareTrigger: Low-stakes challenge — invites a self-assessment reply.

posts.title: The Joyride
posts.hook: Your phone is a getaway car and this city has dogs in it.
posts.script:
The Joyride.
Your phone is the getaway car. Grab the cash, keep it on the road, and dodge everything this city throws at you — cops, people, dogs.
Every hit you take is a wanted star. Rack up too many and you're done, and your crew feels it.
The whole room is driving at once. You can hear it happen — the noise the floor makes when everybody loses at the same corner is genuinely one of my favourite sounds.
Furthest run takes it.
And Problem, if you're watching — put the taco down and drive.
shots: POV windshield, wet neon, speed
a wall of police lights flooding a street
a floor of phones tilting in unison
posts.caption: Cops, people, dogs. Every hit is a star.
posts.shareTrigger: Callback to day 13 — rewards followers who've been there.

posts.title: Crossfire
posts.hook: The whole city is shooting at you and you get three lives.
posts.script:
Crossfire.
Rico's house. Somebody sent targets and now the whole city is shooting at you.
Three lives, that's all you get. Drag, weave, don't get hit. Last one standing in the crossfire owns the night.
This is the loudest the room gets all evening — it's the pink station, it's the hottest music we play, and there is always a moment where four hundred people all flinch at the same time.
Last one standing.
Say goodnight to the bad guy.
shots: neon tracer streaks through pink haze
a white suit unflinching in the storm
a crowd flinching in unison, wide
posts.caption: Three lives. Last one standing owns the night.
posts.shareTrigger: Competitive callout — people tag whoever they'd beat.

posts.title: The Blueprint
posts.hook: You get ten seconds to memorise the vault. Then it's gone.
posts.script:
The Blueprint.
Two plans go up on the screens. Ten seconds each. Burn every icon into your head — and then they're gone, and you have to call them back.
Miss one and the whole job's blown for your crew.
Now — Rico doesn't need the paper. Rico remembers every face that ever crossed him. Rico has told us all repeatedly that his memory is perfect.
Rico cannot remember the first icon.
It's always the falcon. It has been the falcon every single time.
Ten. Nine.
shots: glowing blueprint icons on frosted glass
a falcon icon tapped, macro
phones held up in a dark room
posts.caption: It's always the falcon. Every time. #GTAD
posts.cta: How many can you hold for 10 seconds?
posts.shareTrigger: Testable skill — people want to prove they'd win.

posts.title: The Combination
posts.hook: Everything all night has been building to one code, and it takes all four colours.
posts.script:
This is what the whole night has been for.
The Combination. The vault, in the middle of the room, and one four-colour code that opens it.
Pick your colour. Pick your corner. Black dot means right colour, right spot. White dot means right colour, wrong spot. Crack it before the other three crews do.
It is the loudest, fastest, most unhinged five minutes of the night, and the whole building is screaming numbers at each other.
A glass goes off the podium in slow motion.
And when it hits the floor — every phone in that building starts cracking.
shots: a giant four-colour lock ring glowing
a champagne glass falling, extreme slow-mo
four-colour ballroom, everyone lit up
posts.caption: One code. Four colours. Whoever cracks it first takes the whole thing.
posts.cta: What colour are you cracking for?
posts.shareTrigger: The payoff post — the one to boost paid.

posts.title: Pick Your Colour
posts.hook: There are four crews and you're going to be in one of them. Choose now.
posts.script:
Four crews. You're going to be in one of them.
Gold — the Corvettis. Old money, quiet rooms, nothing written down. You join gold if you think power should be polite.
Pink — Los Halcóns. Loudest crew wins. You join pink if you've never once been the quietest person in a room.
Cyan — the Street Kings. The block, the beat, the bounce. You join cyan if your friends actually like you.
Violet — The Firm. You join violet if you've read the terms and conditions and found a way through them.
Choose now. Because at the door, it's final.
shots: four colour-lit crowd pockets, wide
four wristbands on four wrists
a door, four coloured lights above it
posts.caption: Gold, pink, cyan or violet. At the door it's final. Which one? #GTAD
posts.shareTrigger: THE identity post — the single most shareable format on any platform.

posts.title: Doors
posts.hook: Fifty years that vault's been shut. Tonight all four keys are in the same building.
posts.script:
Fifty years that vault has been shut.
Tonight, for the first time, all four keys are in the same building — and so are all four crews, and so are you.
You know the crews now. You know the vault. You know what it takes to open it.
So here's the last thing I'll say before the doors.
Don't get wasted. Don't get busted. Pick your colour and hold it all night.
And when this city starts lying to you — and it will, from the moment you walk in — the only voice in that room you can trust is coming out of the booth.
That's me. See you tonight.
shots: doors opening onto a neon floor
TJ to camera, hard key, black three-piece
a crowd surging, motion blur
posts.caption: Tonight. All four keys, one building. Don't be late.
posts.cta: Doors at [TIME]. Last tickets in bio.
posts.shareTrigger: Urgency + the catchphrase the audience already knows.
